# Workflow Conventions

## Three workflow files split by triggering event

Verification certifies on PRs; delivery runs on the landing push. `integrate.yml` (triggers `pull_request: [dev]` + `workflow_dispatch`; concurrency `group: integrate-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true` — a superseded PR run cancels whole) runs the entire verify DAG. `publish.yml` (triggers `push: [main, dev]`; concurrency `group: publish-${{ github.ref }}` with NO cancel — the queue is the policy: overlapping `main` releases wait their turn so `publish-stable` can never die mid-release, and queued dev runs guarantee every merge to `dev` gets its prerelease set 1:1) runs the delivery jobs gated by branch: `ensure-release-pr` and `publish-prerelease` on `dev`, `publish-stable` on `main`. `merge-gate.yml` is the third file — the bors-model lander, dual-triggered on the `ready-to-merge` label event (consent wake) and Integrate's green completion (readiness wake, via `workflow_run` — the one sanctioned carve-out of the org-wide delivery-bridge ban: merge-gate's completion wake only; the verb re-asserts the label because the workflow_run payload carries no labels and no PR number), per-PR concurrency group with NO cancel (serialization gives every wake a complete execution; the verb is idempotent); release-devkit's `AGENTS.md` owns the full contract. No other `workflow_run` use (a push run re-verifying what a PR already certified would be double-running) and no `pull_request: [main]` (the standing release PR's head is the dev tip that already ran identical CI; it reports zero checks, and `main` branch protection must require none). The delivery jobs stand alone — a standing release-PR tracking a red `dev` branch is the accurate state.

The verify DAG (`preflight` and `validate-plan` are the two roots; `needs` is transitive — ancestors are never re-listed):

```
mirror-images ──────────────┐
preflight ──────────────────┼→ get-docker-matrix → build-docker → publish-compose
validate-plan ──────────────┤
preflight + validate-plan ──┴→ get-unity-matrix → preflight-unity
```

`mirror-images` as a third parallel root is the one deliberate exception to the two-root DAG: the repo-specific preflight builds the postgres wrapper image, whose `FROM` is a mirror-prefixed base from `workloads/images.lock`, so the mirror namespace must be populated before `preflight` pulls from it — and because `preflight` needs `mirror-images`, a cycle is forbidden, making `mirror-images` a parallel root rather than a child. Build jobs `needs: [preflight, validate-plan]`: the lint/battery root and the plan root fail fast in their own lanes.

## Shared devkit operations: wrapper-installed release-devkit, inline `uv run` for the rest

Shared devkit operations split by consumption model. release-devkit cannot be a project dependency (it sits inside every consumer's own dependency graph), so it is installed onto the runner by `.github/actions/setup-release-devkit` — a one-step composite that clones the devkit at a pinned SHA into `$RUNNER_TEMP/release-devkit`, the only place the SHA appears. Each verb-owning job prepares checkout → `setup-uv` → wrapper → verb, and the verbs are plain run steps (`uv run --project "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-devkit" --locked --no-dev <verb>`) — see release-devkit's `AGENTS.md` for the consumption shape. The `preflight` job (checkout, the repo's one cache-writing setup-uv, wrapper, `lint-ci` run step, then the repo battery) never carries tokens; the `validate-plan` job (checkout-with-tags, restore setup-uv, wrapper, the `validate-plan` run step) is the plan-time gate. `preflight`'s setup-uv is the single cache writer in the file; every other job restores (`save-cache: "false"`). unity-devkit is a PyPI dev-group dependency like the others, so its verbs run inline as `uv run` (version-sourced by `uv.lock`): `get-unity-matrix` runs `uv run compile-check-unity-matrix` (emitting the include matrix plus the license tag), and each `preflight-unity` leg runs `uv run compile-check-unity` inside its `matrix.editor-image` `unityci/editor` container on self-hosted `unity` runners — license restore-or-activate and the UPM cache are verb-internal. Every other devkit (`python-devkit`, `docker-devkit`, `openapi-client-codegen`) is a PyPI dependency the same way: `mirror-images` runs `uv run mirror`; the `preflight` job runs `uv run --no-sync preflight-python` (the python battery) then `uv run --no-sync preflight` (repo-specific checks) then `uv run --no-sync generate-clients --check` (openapi staleness gate); `get-docker-matrix` runs `uv run docker-build-matrix` (one entry per variant, targets grouped by dependency closure — dependents with the base their `additional_contexts: target:` references pull in); `build-docker` and `publish-compose` run repo-local scripts (`build-docker --variant ${{ matrix.variant }} --targets ${{ matrix.targets }}` per leg, QEMU kept). Every `uv run` in the battery auto-syncs internally (`--no-sync` on the outer steps because the battery's first step is the full sync; everything after re-syncs its own context anyway).

## PyPI matrix eliminated — one `release` environment

Both PyPI packages (`placeframe-common`, `placeframe-core-python`) publish from the single `publish-stable` job (and the single `publish-prerelease` job) under one shared `release` environment — no per-package matrix. PyPI's OIDC trusted-publishing `GitHubPublisher` row is keyed by `(owner, repo, workflow_filename, environment)` and linked to projects many-to-many (`project.oidc_publishers`); concrete publishers (established packages) are reused across projects, so one publisher `(placeframe, publish.yml, release)` validates for both packages. The earlier per-package `pypi-<project>` environments and `--only`/`--exclude` splits were based on the disproven "one project per tuple" reading and are gone. The `release` environment carries no protection rules — the `dev` → `main` release-PR is the human gate, which is what lets the dev channel share it without an approval gate (if `release` ever gains required reviewers, the dev channel breaks). CI jobs have no environment. npm trusted publishers are bound to `publish.yml` (one publisher per package, single workflow filename). `publish-stable` has no artifact stapling — placeframe declares no app builds shelves, so its releases carry the release notes only; `create-release` runs inside the command whenever something published.

All workflow logic lives in Python scripts (release-devkit commands as run steps from the wrapper-installed clone, repo-local scripts via `uv run`) — no inline shell conditionals or loops.
